conventions: Versification: the projection carries οἱ δὲ ἀπῆλθον at the head of MAT.20.5, and the ASV translates it at the end of MAT.20.4 as 'And they went their way'. Rule 37 governs both sides — the English is `added` in 20.4, and s001–s003 of 20.5 are three `unrepresented` units, each noting the other verse. A reference comparison reports the 20.5 tokens as disagreements, and that report is not a correction.

Supplied English: a supplied word completing a standing token's own English folds onto that token (20.6 'hour' on the article, rule 102; 20.9 'were hired' on περί, rule 62; 20.12 'but' on the numeral; 20.20 'him' on the participle, rule 74; 20.23 'my' on the anarthrous adjective; 20.34 'their' inside the verb idiom; the repeated function words at 20.5 and 20.19, rule 103). The one `added` unit outside rule 37 is 20.23 'it is for them', where the ASV supplies a whole clause with its own copula and antecedent. That unit names the competing rule 15 reading; rule 77's supplied-antecedent precedent ('him whom', 'him of whom') is the live alternative if it is reopened.
report: Checked all 51 candidate lemma groups, then read the verse dump end to end because the table is keyed by source lemma and cannot see this chapter's two `added` units. No cross-verse split found; patches are empty.

Participial clauses divide on whether the Greek expresses the subject, which is rule 74's own line: 20.2, 20.11 and 20.30 supply the pronoun onto the participle, while 20.8, 20.9, 20.10, 20.17, 20.24 and 20.29 leave the subject word to the expressed token. 20.9/20.10 and 20.17/20.24 write near-identical English on opposite sides of that line, so the difference sits in the source and not in the analysis.

Every `unrepresented` article traces to a determiner slot another token occupies (rules 20, 38, 54), to an article before a name (23), to the ASV writing no determiner (21's determinerless clause), or to an articular infinitive (61). 20.12's τοῖς is rule 32's apposition clause with ἡμῖν expressed; 20.9's οἱ keeps 'they … that' because nothing stands in apposition to it. 20.14 τὸ σόν against 20.15 τοῖς ἐμοῖς is rule 54's own contrast between a relative expansion and an absolute possessive.

Preverbs are consistent under rule 106: 20.20 προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ -> 'came' / 'to him' against 20.25 προσκαλεσάμενος -> 'called … unto him' differ because a dative complement stands in the first and not the second, which is rule 106's own ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς shape; 20.29 keeps 'out' on the participle because 'out' is no part of ἀπό -> 'from'. 20.25 gives 'over' to both governed genitives, keeping its two parallel clauses on one analysis. δηναρίου likewise: 20.2 gives 'for' to the expressed ἐκ, 20.13 to the bare genitive under rule 21.

Supplied English read as one family: six folds (20.6 'hour' on the article under rule 102, 20.9 'were hired' on περί under rule 62, 20.12 'but' on the numeral, 20.20 'him' on the participle under rule 74, 20.23 'my' on the anarthrous adjective, 20.34 'their' inside the verb idiom) against one `added` — 20.23 'it is for them', the only supplied English forming a clause with its own copula and antecedent. All seven supplied junctures convert a participle to a finite clause (rule 88); none is a rule 98 asyndetic seam, and repeated function words at 20.5 and 20.19 are folded rather than `added`.

BSB: all eight listed disagreements are documented convention differences under rules 20, 21, 23, 32, 37, 38 and 54, and rules 32 and 37 say in terms that such a report is not a correction. None is a genuine error, and no accepted edge was changed to move the figure.

One unit left open as recorded: MAT.20.23 t029–t032, `added` under rule 103 with the rule 15 reading named in its note. Rule 77 is arguably the better fit — a headless οἷς expanded with a supplied antecedent is its 'him whom' / 'him of whom' shape, fifteen units to three — but the supplied copula sits outside rule 77, the unit is already hedged as rule 16 requires, and this is a single-verse judgment rather than a split, so I did not rewrite it.

No promotions. The shapes this chapter met are already covered: 20.20 by rule 106's ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς, 20.9 by rule 62's τὰ παρ᾿ ὑμῶν, 20.6 by rule 102. The only uncovered shape is a repeated supplied determiner over coordinate members (20.5 'the sixth and the ninth hour'), one instance with no corpus check behind it, and rule 103 already keeps a rule 7 word out of `added`.
